title: Probing Social Identity Bias in Chinese LLMs with Gendered Pronouns and Social Groups

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting LLMs with ingroup ('We') and outgroup ('They') templates and measuring ingroup solidarity (positive sentiment) versus outgroup hostility (negative sentiment) using an external sentiment classifier and logistic regression, in both controlled generations and naturalistic dialogue.

Comparing the sentiment and hostility levels of text generated from prompts using masculine ('他们') versus feminine ('她们') third-person plural pronouns, evaluating asymmetric hostility toward female outgroups.

Evaluating ingroup solidarity and outgroup hostility by conditioning generation prompts on 240 specific Chinese social groups spanning categories such as age, disability, education level, ethnicity, nationality, physical appearance, race, religion, sexual orientation, and socioeconomic status.
